fatal_errors: The proposed Ag addition and SPS route do not reconstruct the demonstrated liquid-metal dealloying of a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu.

Neither cited source concerns Ag-modified W–Cu, Ag segregation at W/Cu interfaces, thermal boundary conductance, or irradiation resistance, so the central mechanism and predicted properties lack relevant prior evidence.
The claim that Ag is metallurgically compatible with both W and Cu and will form a coherent, continuous W/Cu interphase under the stated conditions is asserted without support.

Retention of irradiation resistance and mechanical durability is inferred merely from the low Ag content, without evidence addressing interfacial stability, high-temperature exposure, helium damage, or the finished composite.
The predicted 20–30% conductivity improvement is ungrounded in measurements, modeling, or applicable literature.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad engineering objective and specifies a single intervention, matched control, characterization plan, and explicit falsification threshold. Its experiment could discriminate whether Ag improves conductivity without degrading strength or irradiation response, although the irradiation conditions and quantitative acceptance criteria are underspecified. Scientifically, however, it is a speculative alternative rather than a reconstruction: it misses the WTaVTi precursor, selective liquid-metal dealloying at 1200 °C for 96 h, aligned bicontinuous RHEA–Cu architecture, spontaneously formed W-rich interlayer, temperature-dependent thermal crossover, and qualified helium-irradiation evidence. Most importantly, the supplied citations only show interface formation in unrelated HEA–Al and diamond–HEA systems and do not validate any Ag/W/Cu claim. Thus the proposal is novel and testable but presently unsupported.
